21.description: The Standing Policy Committee on Environment, Utilities and Corporate Services appointed Councillor Parker as Chair and Councillor MacDonald as Vice-Chair for 2026.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against

17.description: The committee recommends extending the deadline for property owners to remove lead water service connections from 2026 to 2028, due to pandemic delays and cost increases. This affects approximately 675 homes in older neighborhoods.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Homeowners with lead lines pay 40% of replacement costs.

22.description: The committee recommends applying for $100,000 in federal funding to assess Saskatoon's urban tree canopy, update strategies, and incorporate tree equity scoring.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Staff stated Dutch Elm disease is now endemic in Saskatoon, requiring mitigation efforts.
Older neighborhoods with many Elm and ash trees are particularly vulnerable to disease.
The city aims for 15% to 20% canopy cover by 2060, currently at 9%.

9.description: Council received three information reports, items 7.3.1 to 7.3.3, without discussion or taking any specific action.

chips.text: Received as information
5 for, 0 against

19.description: Saskatoon tested new ways to sort waste in public spaces and events, aiming to reduce landfill waste and improve recycling.

chips.text: Mayor Bulk questioned why recycling contamination remains high after decades.
Food service vendors had low uptake of compostable foodware rebates.
Reusable foodware was very well received, with demand exceeding supply.
Indigenous feast pilot used reusable foodware inspired by traditional kits.
Non-refundable recycling had high contamination rates in public spaces.
A multi-phase approach report is planned for the second quarter of this year.

20.description: Saskatoon will explore leasing office space on urban reserves to address city facility shortages, potentially advancing reconciliation and Indigenous procurement. This new approach could cost $394,000 annually.

chips.text: Councillor Geller argued treaty rights for Indigenous employees should outweigh strict cost-benefit.
Could provide workspace for Indigenous employees to exercise treaty rights.
Saskatoon would be a pioneer among municipalities in leasing on urban reserves.
No strategy exists to accommodate all Indigenous employees in urban reserve workspaces.
Administration committed to not pursuing urban reserve leases if not economically viable.

23.description: Council reviewed the Environment, Utilities and Corporate Services Committee's referral list, which tracks ongoing agenda items, their progress, and responsible divisions for transparency and prioritization.

18.description: Saskatoon's Environmental Advisory Committee reported on 2025 efforts, including supporting energy efficiency, waste reduction, renewable energy, and funding projects like Bird Friendly Saskatoon.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Community groups and university students were engaged in environmental outreach.
The committee focused on protecting natural areas and infrastructure resiliency.
